event: Austin ISD begins school consolidation planning (Phase I community open houses in June 2025).
Board approves ACE-model turnaround plans for Burnet, Dobie and Webb middle schools (two Fs on record, third and fourth anticipated) to avoid state intervention.
TEA ratings flag 12 AISD campuses with three consecutive unacceptable ratings; turnaround plans due Nov 21.
District explains that turnaround plans (restart or close/reassign) will shape consolidation choices; Burnet/Webb/Dobie cannot be closed while plans are active.

Draft plan released: 13 closures (Barrington, Becker, Bryker Woods, Dawson, Maplewood, Oak Springs, Palm, Ridgetop, Sunset Valley, Widén, Winn, Bedichek, Martin), International HS to Navarro as a program, districtwide boundaries redrawn, four non-zoned DL campuses (Odom, Pickle, Sánchez, Wooten), Montessori to Govalle, Joslin immersion, Garza to Martin; $25.6M savings claimed; 82% seat-use target.
Board information session on the draft; KUT reports ~$296M of property at stake across the 13 campuses.
Board workshop: trustees ask for Montessori alternatives to Govalle, question the Garza-to-Martin idea and the Becker-to-Galindo shift; 7,200+ comment cards received.

Updated draft: same 13 closures; new grandfathering, program-continuation, sibling and grade-transition transfer policies (+$500K/yr transportation); receiver tweaks (Bedichek more to Mendez, Sunset Valley more to Boone, Mandarin to Wooten).

Superintendent removes Palm, Bryker Woods and Maplewood from the vote and defers districtwide boundary changes to fall 2026; two officials placed on leave amid an integrity investigation; savings estimate falls to ~$20M.

Final 'Recommended School Closures & Programmatic Reassignments' plan released: 10 closures + International HS; all Widén to Rodriguez; Montessori to Reilly; Sánchez/Pickle/Wooten stay zoned with DL strands; Odom non-zoned DL with neighborhood to Pleasant Hill; Joslin and Garza ideas deferred beyond 2026-27.

After a marathon meeting with nearly 3 hours of public comment, board approves 24 turnaround plans, closes 7 F-rated campuses (7-2; Gonzales, de Urioste no) and 3 dual-language campuses (6-3; Whitley Chu also no), Winn/Widén turnaround plans 5-4; 3,796 students reassigned, 6,319 seats cut, $21.5M savings.
Turnaround plans submitted to TEA.
Principal announcements and intention survey sent to families; enrollment clinics Dec 9-17 at Becker, Ridgetop, Winn, Reilly and Sunset Valley.

Superintendent appoints principals for Wooten (Olano), Wooldridge (Martinez), Sánchez (Barrett), Pickle (Schultz), Pecan Springs (Noe), Odom (Navarro) and confirms leaders at Guerrero-Thompson, Rodriguez, Galindo, Blackshear, Andrews, Kealing, Covington and Paredes.

Board meeting: administration unveils the transition plan (Jan 5 hiring freeze, Jan 12-23 family preference survey, Feb 9-13 informal assignments, staff hiring fairs); enrollment 69,198; Oak Springs/Blackshear decision promised by late January.
Austin Current: district has spent/committed ~$95M in 2022 bond money on the closing schools.
Austin City Council (CM Fuentes) directs the city manager to develop a land policy for partnerships on closing school sites by June 1; Widén and Bedichek named.
Community meetings on repurposing Dawson, Widén, Sunset Valley, Ridgetop, Becker and Bedichek land.
Superintendent announces Blackshear will close and merge with Oak Springs in the rebuilt $47.6M Oak Springs campus in January 2028.
Enrollment just over 69,000 (down 3,000+ in a year); deficit projection $49M; ~1,300 affected families yet to indicate enrollment plans.
District publishes repurposing scores for the six surplus sites; community meetings May 13-June 4.
Last day of school at the 10 closing campuses.

Board declares six properties surplus (Sunset Valley sale; Dawson sale; Bedichek land ground lease; Becker adaptive reuse with improvements; Ridgetop adaptive reuse; Widén adaptive reuse without improvements) and, in the same June 18-19 meeting, adopts the $887M 2026-27 budget 7-1 after $205M in cuts.

District postpones districtwide boundary changes to 2028-29; Phase 1 (receiving-campus relief, overcrowding, Marshall MS attendance area) targeted for 2027-28; superintendent says Phase 2 could include more closures.
Community meeting on the future of the land-banked Martin campus.
Superintendent proposes immediate closure of Paredes MS ahead of an expected fourth F.
Community meetings on Winn (July 28) and Barrington (July 29) swing-space use and repurposing.
Board votes 7-2 (de Urioste, Quintana no) to close Paredes MS; ~353 incoming students to Bailey (~55%) and Mendez (~45%); no layoffs.
Boundary Phase 1 timeline refined (delayed by the Paredes closure and bus hubs): open houses Aug 29, Sept 14, Sept 16; recommendations September; board vote October 2026; effective 2027-28.
Preliminary TEA ratings: Burnet and Webb receive fifth consecutive F (takeover trigger); Dobie earns D; Paredes fourth F with closure approved by TEA; district rated B.
First day of 2026-27: 11 schools closed since spring; most Paredes students at Bailey; ~100 high-school bus hubs launched; deficit reported at $95M for 2025-26.
2025-26 deficit revised to $105M; Brooke ES sale ($17M) slips to September; district to borrow $140M in October for cash flow; Bailey needs portables for Paredes students.

Mayor Watson proposes parent petitions to close Burnet and Webb (replacement school in the $158M Burnet building) to avert a district takeover; petition deadlines Oct 15 and Dec 1; appeal deadline Sept 11; TEA decision expected by December.
